content.introduction: The sources describe the Investing.com Earnings Calendar as a tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide, displaying EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results. It helps users track which companies are reporting on any given day, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. The calendar also shows earnings surprises, which occur when a company's reported EPS or Revenue differs from the analyst consensus forecast. The sources do not provide specific details about upcoming earnings reports for today's date, November 1, 2026.

## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.

# Earnings Calendar

Use our Earnings Calendar to track forecasts for quarterly and annual earnings reports as well as actual outcomes from companies worldwide. See previous and actual earnings per share upon release as well as expected EPS prior to release. Read More

## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.

### How do I filter the Earnings Calendar? [...] An earnings surprise occurs when a company's reported EPS or Revenue differs from the analyst consensus forecast. A positive surprise means the company outperformed expectations, while a negative surprise means it underperformed. The Earnings Calendar displays this as the EPS Surprise % and Revenue Surprise % columns, making it easy to spot which companies beat or missed forecasts at a glance.

## How to use the Earnings Calendar?

TradingView’s Earnings Calendar shows the latest and upcoming earnings reports released by companies. As an important indicator of a company’s financial state, earnings per share are one of the most followed metrics among traders, so the calendar above can serve as a powerful tool for analysis.
